The release evidence runner operates as a dual-state automaton: first, it verifies the integrity of the software environment through repository inspection and dependency resolution; second, it collects and archives verifiable artifacts such as command outputs and UI snapshots. These two phases form a feedback loop where environmental consistency ensures artifact validity, while artifact completeness validates environmental fidelity. The system's failure mode occurs when either phase diverges—either due to an unverified environment or unverifiable artifacts. The core mathematical structure resembles a categorical pullback diagram in which the category of valid environments pulls back to the category of verifiable evidence under the constraint of shared dependencies. This duality ensures that launch readiness is neither purely speculative nor arbitrarily empirical.
